Skia / Metal and Core Graphics on the Cintiq

Matched synthetic input and native canvas conditions. Read ordinary short-stroke behavior first, then stress cases and completion outcomes.

Short strokesOverlap stressSustainedFailuresRecommendationEvidence

Physical pen-to-screen latency remains pending

Endpoint: Scheduled sample → first draw start. This is neither drawing completion nor visible ink. Generated 240 Hz replay bypasses Wacom digitizer and driver delivery. A suitable camera is still required to measure physical pen movement through visible pixels. Neither backend is declared a physical-latency winner.

Coverage: partial

141 attempted in the retained matrix of 372 declared runs; 138 accepted; 2 classified failed observations; 231 pending; 1 invalid.

Acceptance means software artifact validation; image quality and native inspection remain separate review gates. Missing cells are shown as pending, never estimated. Failed runs are excluded from accepted percentiles, so completion counts must be read alongside timings.

Current status: implementation ready, acquisition interrupted

The software harness is implemented, tested and inspected on the running native app. The retained comparison contains 138 accepted runs and two classified Core Graphics sustained-completion failures, arranged in 70 complete pairs. Another 232 declared runs still need a valid accepted-or-failed outcome. This is a partial comparison, not the completed 372-run study.

Acquisition stopped when the Sony display disconnected and reconnected, then a small Window Server overlay covered the Cintiq canvas during the restart. The overlay persisted after computer-control attempts; a physical pointer/pen adjustment has been requested. Native guards, timing thresholds and the frozen workload were not weakened. Physical pen-to-screen acquisition remains pending suitable camera equipment and a real-pen input adapter. The original mirrored display arrangement has been restored while acquisition is paused.

What the available results show — provisional

For the larger cached canvas with 5,000 committed strokes, four available matched pairs have median run-level p95 scheduled-to-first-draw-start delays of 19.31 ms for Skia and 1,013.58 ms for Core Graphics. The fifth pair remains pending. This is software backlog evidence for this implementation and workload, not an optical latency measurement.

The simpler empty cached canvas gives a different picture: the two available larger-canvas pairs have median run-level p95 values of 10.69 ms for Skia and 5.72 ms for Core Graphics. A lower drawing-start delay does not establish earlier visible ink, especially when rasterization is deferred.

Two larger-canvas sustained repeated-overlap pairs have completed Skia runs and failed Core Graphics terminal draws. The completed Skia runs still have approximately 302 ms median run-level p95 delay, so completion alone does not establish responsive drawing. Ordinary short strokes and this adversarial long-stroke retracing must remain separate. Finish the matrix before choosing the next implementation candidate; permanent selection and physical-latency ranking remain open.

Hardware, matching and timing boundaries

Measured native binary: source 8a26d1d7a25bfcbc526584d386a4f49c30ecbbcf, SHA-256 9e7ad2880182ab4ea5416cff763f417fde59a31dab4a992d1d0faad27cb2c16d. Collector frozen separately at acabb64. Apple M2 Pro with 19 GPU cores; macOS 27.0.1 (26A434); Cintiq Pro 22, 3840×2160 physical pixels, 1920×1080 points, nominal 120 Hz. Measured canvases are 1600×1000 and 2560×1600 physical pixels. The Sony secondary display was unmirrored during retained trials.

Both adapters consume the same timestamped generated 240 Hz trace through shared Rust editing and geometry. Both use the same application-controlled R full-redraw or C cached-base-plus-live policy, synchronous cache replacement, canvas dimensions and input-preservation rules. The replay bypasses Wacom digitizer and driver delivery; Pro Pen 3 is owner-reported, not characterized by these trials.

The primary delay ends at the start of the first drawing callback representing each input sample. It excludes the remainder of drawing, deferred rasterization, composition, scanout and pixel response. All-sample delays expose backlog that latest-sample age alone can hide. A nominal 120 Hz mode and Metal callbacks do not measure photons.

Verification and diagnostic evidence

The integration check, 20 experiment tests, strict experiment Clippy and release build passed at native revision 8a26d1d. All 49 portable analysis/report tests passed after report integration at f3dc920. The final report narrative changes are checked separately; native measurements are never relabeled as a report-only revision.

Fifty-six separately identified two-second visual/ledger pilots passed at native revision 8756358: seven workload cases, two canvas sizes, both policies and both backends. Within each backend, R/C final images were byte-identical for all 28 matched pairs. Cross-backend edge antialiasing differs; scene geometry, orientation, scale and clipping were inspected rather than demanding pixel identity.

Native inspection at 8a26d1d covered Ready/Completed states, both physical canvas sizes, Run, Escape, Command-period cancellation, Command-Q preservation/exit and Show Results availability. A designer reviewed source, screenshots and those observations. Dark appearance, complete keyboard focus traversal, physical pen feel and temporal cache handoff appearance remain unverified.

Three paired logging-overhead trials per backend and four native Stop tests passed in separate preflight evidence. Full-versus-minimal CPU differences were small and mixed; this does not prove zero logging overhead. Every comparative run uses full logging.

An excluded 90-second diagnostic at the same native revision sampled the stalled Core Graphics main thread in backing-store/display-list rasterization and antialiasing edge distribution. This explains why short draw callbacks can coexist with high process CPU and input backlog. The profile is diagnostic, not an additional comparative timing trial. Process CPU includes app-side deferred rasterization but excludes WindowServer CPU and GPU execution.

A fresh reviewer independently regenerated the partial analysis, verified all 140 retained outcomes against prior-session artifact hashes, checked the recovery chain and confirmed one identical dual-display inventory stratum. The final partial report has no outstanding review blocker. The designer approved its source and opening screenshot as a partial report; the lead checked browser layout and narrow-screen overflow.

Recovery history and evidence retention

All halted sessions remain preserved. Three environmental attempts were rejected across sessions: a transient Dock overlay, the Sony display configuration change, and the small Window Server overlay. An otherwise accepted Skia run from the interrupted pair is retained as an unpaired excluded run. It is not relabeled invalid. Both members of that pair must be repeated together.

The two classified sustained failures are preserved as failed and are not retried. Their input completeness, final expected hashes and artifact receipts were verified under the explicitly recorded continuation policy. Other failures and visibility changes halt acquisition. The current coverage counter describes the latest collection, including imported complete pairs; it does not count every historical attempt.

Raw ledgers, receipts, manifests, images, all four collection sessions, recovery records and the separately identified preflight/profile evidence remain in local artifacts. The downloadable analysis preserves accepted runs, failed observations, every declared pair outcome, uncertainty summaries and frozen provenance. Source benchmark contracts record the protocol amendment. The previously stopped bundle-size checks have not been resumed.

1. Ordinary short-stroke traces

Separate 0.75-second strokes. Cached rendering is shown first; full redraw is a control. Warm, first-painter-use and after-idle runs, and the two physical canvas sizes, stay separate. “Ordinary” describes this generated trace shape, not a measurement of real pen feel. First-painter-use values summarize the full 30-second replay and can dilute a one-time first-mark cost; reference construction and context initialization precede that replay epoch. These are not cold-launch-to-visible-ink measurements.

Failed observations remain visible

A separately frozen opt-in collector policy permits continuation only for the exact sustained terminal-paint watchdog after input completeness, final expected hashes, source, configuration, display and lifecycle checks. The native watchdog is unchanged. Stop, visibility changes and other failures still halt collection.

Failure gaps include the censored interval from the last draw to finish entry. Undrawn sample ages are measured at that endpoint, not photons or observed first-draw latencies. Failed runs are excluded from accepted percentiles. Empty failure tables mean no classified failure in this analysis, not proof that every pending run will succeed.

Recommendation and remaining decision

Comparison recommendation pending. Collection or validation is incomplete. Do not choose a backend from the currently available subset, or interpret missing cells as successful runs.

Synchronous cache replacement queues incoming input during rebuilds in both adapters. Asynchronous replacement is deferred. Physical pen-to-screen latency remains pending a suitable camera regardless of software results.

ApproachAdvantagesCosts and limits
Skia / MetalExplicit GPU submission and separate Metal observations; potential renderer reuse across platforms.Additional bundled engine and GPU resources. Drawable waits and queueing matter; Metal callbacks do not measure photons.
AppKit / Core GraphicsSystem drawing API and native AppKit integration without bundling Skia.Drawing can be deferred beyond callback return. A short draw callback omits deferred rasterization. Process CPU includes work performed in this app, but excludes WindowServer CPU and GPU execution.

Expandable evidence: every run and pair

All declared outcomes are retained, including both-failed pairs. Numeric timing differences exist only when both runs are accepted. Accepted/failed combinations are checked for matching input, canvas and power conditions.

Measured process CPU and callback wall time

Process user and system CPU sum execution across all process threads from the measured replay epoch to finish entry. They exclude initialization, warm-up, idle, GPU retirement, capture and artifact serialization. External WindowServer CPU and GPU execution are not included. Draw callback totals are synchronous wall durations including drawable waits and painter calls; they are not CPU utilization. RSS is process-lifetime peak memory including initialization and untimed capture, excluding distinct GPU/WindowServer allocations. Missing values remain unknown (—), never zero. These are descriptive measurements, not energy estimates.

Measurement limits

Skipped drawing snapshots are not lost input samples: acceptance requires every expected sample in the delivery ledger and a subsequent first drawing representation. Frame input timing fields are not summed as Rust work; host aggregate advance totals are retained. Final captures are untimed painter/readback proxies, not proof of presented pixels. OS visibility flags do not establish absence of every partial occluder. Visibility checks run on the main queue and can miss transient occlusion while that queue is blocked; they are not continuous proof of visibility. A nominal display refresh rate is not an observed pen-to-screen latency or a performance budget.
